faith.name: Shintō
faith.description: Shintō is the native faith of the islands — the way of the kami who inhabit mountain, river, rice-paddy and ancestor. Every village keeps a shrine to its local kami; every household honours Amaterasu, ruling kami of the Heavenly Plain, from whom the Imperial line descends.
faith.blessing_action: Kannushi, I would have a blessing of the kami.
faith.blessing_question: Which kami's blessing do you seek?
faith.blessing_confirm_question: Will you bear the kami's mark?

faith.name: Rinzai Zen
faith.description: The Rinzai school is the Zen of the kōan — sudden insight forced by the master's stick and the impossible question. Of all the Buddhist schools the daimyō favour Rinzai most, for its discipline turns easily into the discipline of the sword.
faith.blessing_action: Rōshi, I would receive a teaching.
faith.blessing_question: Whose lineage do you wish to receive?
faith.blessing_confirm_question: Will you sit with the master's word?

faith.name: Sōtō Zen
faith.description: The Sōtō school teaches that practice and enlightenment are not two — sit zazen, and you are already a Buddha. Its mother house Eiheiji stands in the snows of Echizen, and its abbots refuse the patronage games of the capital.
faith.blessing_action: Zenji, I would receive a teaching.
faith.blessing_confirm_question: Will you give the cushion the time it asks?

faith.name: Shingon
faith.description: The Shingon school is the esoteric Buddhism of Kūkai — mantra, mudra and mandala. The cosmos itself is the body of Dainichi Buddha, and the practitioner who traces the mandala traces him. Its high seat is Mount Kōya, and its warrior-monks have defended it through every war.
faith.blessing_action: Daiajari, I seek an esoteric blessing.
faith.blessing_question: Through which Buddha's aspect will the blessing pass?
faith.blessing_confirm_question: Will you carry the mantra to the end of your days?

faith.name: Tendai
faith.description: The Tendai school is the great syncretism of Mount Hiei — Lotus Sūtra, esoteric ritual and Zen practice woven together. Its head abbot, the Zasu, is one of the great religious lords of the realm, and its sōhei warrior-monks have ridden into the capital itself when the school's interests required it.
faith.blessing_action: Zasu, I seek a teaching of the Lotus.
faith.blessing_question: Through which aspect of the One Vehicle?
faith.blessing_confirm_question: Will you read the Lotus all your days?

faith.name: Jōdo Shinshū
faith.description: The Shin school teaches the single practice: trust in Amida's vow and recite his name. Its priests marry, its laity rule themselves through the kō, and when the Monshu speaks the Ikkō-Ikki rises — leagues of farmers and ji-samurai under a single religious banner.
faith.blessing_action: Monshu, I would recite the Nembutsu.
faith.blessing_question: How long will you carry the name?
faith.blessing_confirm_question: Will you say the name daily?
